items.hook: The Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified, guaranteeing women's suffrage.
items.body: The Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution prohibits the United States and its states from denying the right to vote to citizens of the United States on the basis of sex, in effect recognizing the right of women to vote. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Major Gordon Laing becomes the first European to enter Timbuktu.
items.body: Major Alexander Gordon Laing was a Scottish explorer and the first European to reach Timbuktu, arriving there via the north-to-south route in August 1826. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The City Outside the World is a science fantasy novel by American writer Lin Carter, the third in his Edgar Rice Burroughs- and Leigh Brackett-inspired series The Mysteries of Mars.
items.body: It was first published in paperback by Berkley Medallion in October 1977 and in reissued in trade paperback by Wildside Press in December 1999. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: There Was Still Love is a 2019 novel by Favel Parrett.
items.body: The novel follows two Czechoslovak sisters, one of whom relocates to Australia while the other stays in Prague. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Rêveuse bourgeoisie is a 1937 novel by the French writer Pierre Drieu La Rochelle.
items.body: It tells the story of a declining middle-class family before and after World War I, told in five parts which span over three generations. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Iceland's Bell is a historical novel by Nobel Prize-winning Icelandic author Halldór Kiljan Laxness.
items.body: It was published in three parts: Iceland's Bell (1943), The Bright Jewel or The Fair Maiden (1944) and Fire in Copenhagen (1946). One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Civil rights movement: James Meredith becomes the first African American to graduate from the University of Mississippi.
items.body: The civil rights movement was a social movement in the United States from 1954 to 1968 which aimed to abolish legalized racial segregation, discrimination, and disenfranchisement in the country, which most commonly affected African Americans. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.body: The Siege of Baghdad was a fifty-day blockade of Baghdad, the seat of the Abbasid caliphs, in 1136. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Formerly a wife of deity Thongalen, later adopted by Koupalu, she finally married Luwang dynasty prince Nungpan Ponpi Luwaopa, and mothered Luwang Ningthou Punshiba.
